entry.name: qlist
entry.description: Stores a collection of timed or untimed "cues" in the form of messages which can be sent either out its outlet or remotely to various receive objects in your patch.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: Double-clicking with the mouse on theobject displays its contents as text in an editing window which the user can modify.

messages.name: append
messages.digest: Append a message to the last entry
messages.description: The wordfollowed by any arguments will append those arguments to the last entry in theobject's cue-list. To append a semicolon, it must be preceded by a backslash character.

messages.name: bang
messages.description: Sending ato qlist triggers automatic-playback of the entire cue list. It begins sending messages from the first line, until a line begins with a number, at which pointwill use that number as a delay time in milliseconds before continuing to send the remaining messages. Athat is playing automatically can be stopped using themessage.

messages.name: clear
messages.description: The wordwill clear the contents of the cue-list. This is the same as sending amessage with no arguments.

messages.name: fwd
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, is used to "fast forward" through a given number of lines, without remotely sending messages to named receive objects. For example,will output the next two lines in the cue-list which bengin with numerical values. Lines beginning with symbols will be ignored.

messages.name: insert
messages.description: The wordfollowed by any arguments will append those arguments to theobject's cue-list as a new entry in the list. To append a semicolon, it must be preceded by a backslash character.

messages.name: next
messages.description: The wordis used to output the next line in the cue-list. It will remotely send all lines beginning with a symbol, and stop after it encounters and outputs a line beginning with a numerical value. If the wordis followed by a non-zero argument, it will ignore lines beginning with symbols and only output the next line beginning with a numerical value.

messages.name: open
messages.description: The wordwill cause theobject's text editing window to be opened.

messages.name: read
messages.description: The wordwill allow you to read a file from disk via a standard Max file opening dialog. If followed by a symbol argument, Max will use the symbol as a filename (or filepath and filename) and try to read a text file with the given name from the disk.

messages.name: rewind
messages.digest: Move to the beginning of the file

messages.name: set
messages.description: The wordcan be used to set the contents of aobject. It completely clears any previous cue-list contents. Sending amessage with no arguments is the same as sending amessage.

messages.name: stop
messages.description: The wordcan be used to stop awhich is in the middle of playback as a result of amessage.

messages.name: tempo
messages.description: The word, followed by a floating-point numerical value, can be used to allow ato automatically play itself at a faster or slower speed than indicated by the millisecond values stored internally in the cue list. By default the tempo is 1.0, which means the playback tempo is not scaled. A tempo of 0.5 plays back the cue list at half speed, whereas a tempo of 2. plays it back twice as fast.

messages.name: wclose
messages.description: The wordwill cause theobject's text editing window to be closed.

messages.name: write
messages.description: The wordwill allow you to save a file via a standard Max file saving dialog. If followed by a symbol argument, Max will use the symbol as a filename (or filepath and filename) and write a text file with the given name to disk.
